ablation.kurz: Removal of material by laser irradiation.
ablation.definition: In laser ablation material is removed by evaporation, melt ejection, spallation or plasma processes. It sets in above the [[ablationsschwelle|ablation threshold]].

ablationsschwelle.kurz: Fluence above which material removal sets in (material specific).
ablationsschwelle.definition: The ablation threshold is the [[fluenz]] above which material removal sets in. It is material specific. Derivation and determination follow in chapter K07.

abschwaecher.kurz: Component for continuous adjustment of the pulse energy.
abschwaecher.definition: Common: a rotatable half-wave plate in front of a polarizer. The laser itself remains unchanged.

absorption.kurz: Uptake of light energy by the material.
absorption.definition: In absorption the light gives energy to the material (excitation of electrons or lattice vibrations). Together with [[reflexion]] and [[transmission]], $A+R+T=1$ holds.

absorptionskoeffizient.kurz: Attenuation of the intensity per path length, $\alpha$ in 1/m (or 1/cm).
absorptionskoeffizient.definition: The absorption coefficient $\alpha$ describes the attenuation in the Beer–Lambert law $I(z)=I_0e^{-\alpha z}$. Its inverse is the [[eindringtiefe|penetration depth]].

abstract.kurz: Short summary of an article: aim, method, result, conclusion.
abstract.definition: The abstract decides whether you read an article. When reading, a good order is: abstract, figures, conclusion, then methods.

abtragrate.kurz: Removed volume per time, e.g. in mm³/min.
abtragrate.definition: The removal rate $\dot V$ follows from volume per pulse and repetition rate. Relative to the power one obtains the efficiency in mm³/(min·W).

autokorrelation.kurz: Pulse duration measurement in which the pulse is superimposed with a time-delayed copy of itself.
autokorrelation.definition: In an intensity autocorrelation a pulse is split, delayed in time and superimposed in a nonlinear crystal (SHG). The width of the signal over the delay is $\tau_\mathrm{AC}=\kappa\,\tau$, with $\kappa=\sqrt2$ for Gaussian pulses. The pulse shape has to be assumed.

avalanche-ionisation.kurz: Avalanche-like multiplication of free charge carriers.
avalanche-ionisation.definition: In avalanche ionization a free electron absorbs laser energy and creates further free electrons by collision, so that their number grows like an avalanche. Seed electrons come e.g. from [[multiphotonenabsorption]].

axicon.kurz: Conical optical element that generates a Bessel beam.
axicon.definition: An axicon produces a long, narrow focal line with which glass can be modified through its full thickness.

bandluecke.kurz: Energy range without electron states between valence and conduction band, $E_\mathrm{g}$.
bandluecke.definition: The band gap $E_\mathrm{g}$ separates the valence band from the conduction band. Photons with less energy cannot excite the material through a single absorption; dielectrics are therefore transparent in the visible and near infrared. Metals have no band gap.

bessel-strahl.kurz: Beam shaping for cutting glass through the full thickness.
bessel-strahl.definition: Bessel beam and filamentation are beam-shaping concepts with which glass can be cut through its full thickness.

beugung.kurz: Spreading of waves around obstacles and through apertures; limits the focus size.
beugung.definition: Because of diffraction light cannot be focused arbitrarily sharply; the smallest focus is of the order of the wavelength. Diffraction-limited means $M^2\approx1$.

bpp.kurz: Product of waist radius and divergence half-angle, $\mathrm{BPP}=w_0\theta=M^2\lambda/\pi$.
bpp.definition: The beam parameter product $\mathrm{BPP}=w_0\theta$ is conserved in lossless beam shaping with ideal optics and characterizes the beam quality. For the ideal Gaussian beam $\mathrm{BPP}=\lambda/\pi$. Usual unit: mm·mrad.

brechungsindex.kurz: Ratio of the vacuum speed of light to the phase velocity in the material, $n=c/v$.
brechungsindex.definition: The refractive index $n$ determines how strongly light is refracted and delayed in the material. Together with the extinction coefficient $\kappa$ it forms the complex refractive index $\tilde n=n+\mathrm{i}\kappa$. It depends on the wavelength ([[dispersion]]).

brennweite.kurz: Distance between lens and focus for parallel incident light, $f$.
brennweite.definition: The focal length $f$ determines, together with wavelength, $M^2$ and beam radius on the lens, the focus size: $w_0\approx M^2\lambda f/(\pi w_\mathrm{in})$.

bruchzaehigkeit.kurz: Resistance of a material to crack propagation, $K_\mathrm{Ic}$.
bruchzaehigkeit.definition: The fracture toughness $K_\mathrm{Ic}$ (unit MPa√m) states at which stress intensity an existing crack grows unstably. Ceramics have low values, metals high ones.

burst-mode.kurz: Pulse packets instead of single pulses.
burst-mode.definition: In burst mode, pulse packets are emitted instead of single pulses, with pulse spacings down to the GHz range. According to the project notes this increases removal rate and efficiency.

chirp.kurz: Change of the instantaneous frequency within a pulse over time.
chirp.definition: A pulse is chirped if its instantaneous frequency rises or falls along the pulse, e.g. after dispersion. At the same bandwidth a chirped pulse is longer than the Fourier-limited pulse.

coulomb-explosion.kurz: Ions are repelled from a positively charged surface and ejected.
coulomb-explosion.definition: When many electrons leave the surface it stays positively charged; the electrostatic repulsion can eject ions and small clusters. Discussed for dielectrics and semiconductors near the threshold.

cpa.kurz: Amplification of stretched pulses, the basis of all high-power UKP systems.
cpa.definition: In chirped pulse amplification (CPA) the pulse is stretched in time, amplified and compressed again. According to the project notes it is the basis of all high-power UKP systems. Details follow in chapter K04.

d2-methode.kurz: Determining threshold and beam radius from the square of the crater diameter versus $\ln E_\mathrm{p}$.
d2-methode.definition: According to Liu (1982), $D^2=2w_0^2\ln(E_\mathrm{p}/E_\mathrm{th})$. A straight line in the $D^2$–$\ln E_\mathrm{p}$ diagram gives $w_0$ from the slope and the threshold energy from the zero crossing.

debris.kurz: Redeposited ablation material around the processed spot.
debris.definition: Debris consists of particles, droplets and condensate. It degrades edge quality and roughness and is reduced by extraction or shielding gas.

dielektrikum.kurz: Electrical insulator with a large band gap, usually transparent in the visible.
dielektrikum.definition: Dielectrics such as fused silica and sapphire absorb light in the visible and near infrared only through nonlinear processes. That makes volume processing possible.

diffusionslaenge.kurz: Distance that heat travels in the time $\tau$, $L_\mathrm{th}\approx\sqrt{D\tau}$.
diffusionslaenge.definition: If $L_\mathrm{th}$ is smaller than the [[eindringtiefe|penetration depth]], the energy stays in the absorption volume: hardly any heat-affected zone.

dispersion.kurz: Dependence of the refractive index on wavelength, which stretches pulses in time.
dispersion.definition: Because of dispersion, different frequency components of a pulse travel at different speeds. The group delay dispersion (GDD, $\varphi_2$ in fs²) describes the second-order effect. Positive GDD stretches a pulse, negative GDD can shorten it again.

divergenz.kurz: Widening of the beam with distance, half-angle $\theta$.
divergenz.definition: The divergence of a Gaussian beam is $\theta=M^2\lambda/(\pi w_0)$. A small focus means large divergence.

doe-element.kurz: Optic that shapes or splits the beam by diffraction.
doe-element.definition: DOEs produce e.g. top-hat profiles or several beams for parallel processing.

doi.kurz: Persistent identifier of an article, resolvable via doi.org.
doi.definition: A DOI has the form 10.xxxx/yyyy. It should be in every literature entry and is the most reliable way to find an article again.

eigenspannung.kurz: Mechanical stress in a component without external load.
eigenspannung.definition: Residual stresses arise e.g. from non-uniform heating and cooling or from local modification (volume change). In glass and ceramics they can trigger cracks.

eindringtiefe.kurz: Depth at which the intensity has dropped to $1/e$, $\delta=1/\alpha$.
eindringtiefe.definition: The (optical) penetration depth $\delta=1/\alpha$ determines in which layer the energy is absorbed. A small $\delta$ means high energy density and a low threshold.

elektron-phonon-kopplung.kurz: Energy transfer from the electrons to the lattice, constant $G$.
elektron-phonon-kopplung.definition: The coupling determines how fast the electron and lattice systems equalize (time scale of a few picoseconds). It enters the two-temperature model as $G(T_\mathrm{e}-T_\mathrm{l})$.

f-theta.kurz: Scan lens in which the position is proportional to the deflection angle, $x=f\theta$.
f-theta.definition: The f-theta lens focuses onto a flat field and fixes focus size and working field (both $\propto f$).

faserlaser.kurz: Laser with a doped glass fibre as the gain medium.
faserlaser.definition: Fibre lasers are compact, robust and easy to cool; the high intensity in the small fibre core limits the pulse energy through nonlinearities.

fluenz.kurz: Pulse energy per area in J/cm², central process quantity.
fluenz.definition: The fluence $F=E_\mathrm{p}/A$ is the pulse energy delivered per area, here in J/cm². It is the central process quantity; ablation sets in above the [[ablationsschwelle]]. For a [[gauss-strahl]] one distinguishes the peak fluence $F_0$ from the mean fluence.

fokuslage.kurz: Position of the focus relative to the workpiece surface.
fokuslage.definition: The focus position $z$ is a process parameter of its own: even small deviations change the peak fluence. In depth ablation it is tracked.

fourier-limit.kurz: Shortest pulse duration for a given spectrum, without chirp.
fourier-limit.definition: A transform-limited pulse satisfies $\tau\Delta\nu=K$. Any chirp makes the pulse longer.

frequenz.definition: The frequency $\nu$ states how often the light wave oscillates per second. For light of 1030 nm, $\nu=c/\lambda\approx2.9\cdot10^{14}\,\mathrm{Hz}$. Do not confuse it with the repetition rate of a laser.

fresnel.kurz: Reflectance and transmittance at an interface, depending on angle and polarization.
fresnel.definition: The Fresnel equations give reflection and transmission at the interface of two media, depending on the angle of incidence, the [[polarisation|polarization]] and the (complex) [[brechungsindex|refractive index]].

frog.kurz: Method for reconstructing the amplitude and phase of a pulse.
frog.definition: FROG measures a spectrogram (spectrally resolved autocorrelation) and provides pulse shape and chirp, unlike plain [[autokorrelation|autocorrelation]].

galvo-scanner.kurz: Two fast mirrors that deflect the beam.
galvo-scanner.definition: Together with an [[f-theta]] lens it reaches scan speeds in the m/s range. Inertia and acceleration limit the contour accuracy.

gauss-strahl.kurz: Beam with a Gaussian intensity profile, described by the beam radius $w_0$.
gauss-strahl.definition: A Gaussian beam has the radial intensity profile $I(r)=I_0\,e^{-2r^2/w_0^2}$. The [[strahlradius]] $w_0$ is the radius at which the intensity has dropped to $1/e^2$ of the maximum.

gdd.definition: The GDD $\varphi_2$ describes how the group delay changes with frequency. It determines how strongly a pulse is stretched in time by a material.

gitter.kurz: Periodic arrangement of the atoms in a solid.
gitter.definition: In the two-temperature model “lattice” stands for the system of atomic cores and their vibrations ([[phonon|phonons]]), as opposed to the electron system.

halbleiter.kurz: Material with a small band gap; conductivity between metal and insulator.
halbleiter.definition: In semiconductors the ratio of photon energy to band gap decides whether absorption is linear. Examples: silicon, silicon carbide.

halbwertsbreite.kurz: Width of a curve at half of its maximum value.
halbwertsbreite.definition: The full width at half maximum (FWHM) is the full width of a distribution at half height. For pulses the FWHM of the intensity is usually given, for the beam diameter often the $1/e^2$ diameter. For a Gaussian profile $d_\mathrm{FWHM}=w\sqrt{2\ln2}\approx1.18\,w$.

hatch.kurz: Distance between adjacent scan tracks in area ablation.
hatch.definition: The hatch $h$ is the spacing of the scan lines in area ablation. Together with the pulse spacing it determines the pulse number per area, the accumulated fluence and the area rate $\dot A=v\,h$.

haz.kurz: Edge region altered by heat; minimal with UKP.
haz.definition: The heat-affected zone (HAZ) is the region next to the processed spot whose microstructure or properties were changed by heat. With UKP it is considered minimal.

inkubation.kurz: Lowering of the ablation threshold by preceding pulses.
inkubation.definition: In the incubation effect the [[ablationsschwelle]] falls when the same spot has already been hit by earlier pulses.

intensitaet.kurz: Power per area in W/cm²; for pulses approximately $F/\tau$.
intensitaet.definition: The intensity $I$ is the power per area (here W/cm²). For a pulse $I\approx F/\tau$ holds approximately. Nonlinear effects such as [[multiphotonenabsorption]] depend on the intensity, not on the fluence.

interferenz.kurz: Superposition of waves: reinforcement or cancellation depending on phase.
interferenz.definition: Interference arises when coherent waves are superimposed. Examples in laser processing: autocorrelation, [[lipss]] and diffractive optics.

ionisation.kurz: Release of electrons from bound states.
ionisation.definition: In a dielectric ionization means the excitation of an electron from the [[valenzband|valence band]] into the [[leitungsband|conduction band]]. Mechanisms: multiphoton, tunnel and impact ionization.

keldysh-parameter.kurz: Number $\gamma$ that distinguishes multiphoton ($\gamma\gg1$) from tunnel ionization ($\gamma\ll1$).
keldysh-parameter.definition: The Keldysh parameter $\gamma$ compares the laser frequency with the tunnelling frequency of an electron in the deformed potential barrier. For $\gamma\gg1$ multiphoton ionization dominates, for $\gamma\ll1$ tunnel ionization. The transition region lies at $\gamma$ close to $1$ to $2$.

keramik.kurz: Inorganic, non-metallic, mostly polycrystalline and brittle material.
keramik.definition: Technical ceramics (e.g. aluminium oxide, silicon nitride) are hard, wear-resistant and temperature-resistant, but [[spoedigkeit|brittle]] and sensitive to [[thermoschock|thermal shock]].

knife-edge.kurz: Beam radius measurement by moving an edge through the beam.
knife-edge.definition: The radius follows from the transmitted power: $w=\Delta x_{10\text{–}90}/1.28$ for a Gaussian beam.

kohaerenz.kurz: Fixed phase relationship of the light wave over time (temporal) or space (spatial).
kohaerenz.definition: Laser light is coherent: the phases are correlated over large distances. This enables sharp focusing and interference.

kollimation.definition: A collimated beam has an almost constant radius over a long distance. Before focusing, the beam is usually collimated and expanded.

kompressor.kurz: Dispersive arrangement with negative GDD that shortens the pulse again.
kompressor.definition: Usually a grating pair. The compressor has to cancel the total dispersion of the system; it is often placed behind the amplifier.

krater.kurz: Depression that one or several pulses leave in the material.
krater.definition: The crater diameter $D$ is used in the [[d2-methode|D² method]] to determine threshold and beam radius.

kritische-dichte.kurz: Electron density at which the plasma frequency equals the laser frequency: $n_\mathrm{c}=\varepsilon_0m_\mathrm{e}\omega^2/e^2$.
kritische-dichte.definition: When a plasma reaches the critical density $n_\mathrm{c}$, it shields the laser light and absorbs or reflects strongly. For $\lambda=1030\,\mathrm{nm}$, $n_\mathrm{c}\approx1\cdot10^{21}\,\mathrm{cm^{-3}}$.

lambert-beer.kurz: Exponential decay of the intensity in the material, $I=I_0e^{-\alpha z}$.
lambert-beer.definition: The Beer–Lambert law describes linear absorption: the intensity falls exponentially with the depth $z$. It no longer holds for nonlinear absorption, because $\alpha$ then depends on the intensity.

laser.kurz: Light source that produces coherent light by stimulated emission.
laser.definition: Laser stands for light amplification by stimulated emission of radiation. A gain medium in a [[resonator]] produces coherent, usually narrow-band light with low divergence.

leitungsband.kurz: Energetically higher electron band, empty in the ground state (insulator, semiconductor).
leitungsband.definition: Electrons in the conduction band are mobile and absorb light as free carriers. In metals the conduction band is partly filled.

lipss.kurz: Self-organized periodic nanostructures on the surface.
lipss.definition: LIPSS (laser-induced periodic surface structures) are self-organized, periodic nanostructures that form on the surface under laser irradiation.

m2.kurz: Measure of beam quality: $M^2=1$ is ideally Gaussian, larger values focus worse.
m2.definition: The beam propagation factor $M^2\ge1$ is the ratio of the beam parameter product (BPP) of a real beam to that of the ideal Gaussian beam. It is determined according to ISO 11146 from the second moments of the intensity distribution. A high $M^2$ enlarges the focus or shrinks the Rayleigh length for the same optics.

messunsicherheit.kurz: Range in which the true value of a measured quantity is expected.
messunsicherheit.definition: Uncorrelated relative uncertainties are added in quadrature. For the fluence the beam radius enters twice: $\delta F/F=\sqrt{(\delta E/E)^2+(2\delta w/w)^2}$.

mittlere-leistung.definition: The average power $P_\mathrm{avg}=E_\mathrm{p}\cdot f$ is pulse energy times repetition rate. It determines the heat load and the throughput, not the peak load on the material.

modenkopplung.kurz: Fixed phase locking of the cavity modes, so that a short pulse circulates in the cavity.
modenkopplung.definition: In mode locking all longitudinal cavity modes oscillate with a fixed phase relationship. Their superposition is a pulse that passes through the cavity with the round-trip time $2L/c$. The more modes (bandwidth), the shorter the pulse.

multiphotonenabsorption.kurz: Simultaneous absorption of several photons in transparent media.
multiphotonenabsorption.definition: In multiphoton absorption several photons take up energy at the same time, although each single [[photonenenergie|photon]] has too little energy for the band gap. It is a nonlinear process and only relevant at high [[intensitaet]] (Keldysh theory).

nichtthermischer-abtrag.kurz: Ablation where the energy reaches the lattice before heat can flow away.
nichtthermischer-abtrag.definition: “Non-thermal” is a limiting case: even with UKP the energy ends up as heat, but the heat-affected zone stays small because there is no time for diffusion.

oszillator.kurz: Mode-locked laser that produces the short seed pulse.
oszillator.definition: The oscillator delivers pulses in the nanojoule range at a high rate (e.g. 100 MHz). It is the first building block of a [[cpa]] system.

peer-review.kurz: Expert evaluation of a manuscript by independent specialists before publication.
peer-review.definition: Peer review safeguards the quality of scientific articles but does not guarantee correctness. Preprints are not peer reviewed.

phasenexplosion.kurz: Sudden decay of superheated melt into vapour and droplets.
phasenexplosion.definition: In a phase explosion (explosive boiling) the melt is superheated to temperatures near the critical temperature and decays into a mixture of vapour and droplets. Typical at fluences well above the threshold.

phonon.definition: Phonons are the quasi-particles of lattice vibrations. Hot electrons give energy to the lattice via [[elektron-phonon-kopplung|electron–phonon coupling]].

photon.definition: A photon is the energy quantum of light. It carries the energy $h\nu=hc/\lambda$ and the momentum $p=h/\lambda$.

photonenenergie.definition: A photon of wavelength $\lambda$ carries the energy $h\nu=hc/\lambda\approx 1239.84\ \mathrm{eV\,nm}/\lambda$. Whether a single photon can bridge the band gap of a material decides between linear and [[multiphotonenabsorption]].

plasma.kurz: Ionized gas or electron gas of high density that behaves like a metal.
plasma.definition: At high electron density (after multiphoton ionization and avalanche) the excited material behaves like a plasma: it absorbs and reflects light differently from the starting material.

plasmafrequenz.kurz: Natural frequency of the electron gas, $\omega_\mathrm{p}^2=n_\mathrm{e}e^2/(\varepsilon_0m_\mathrm{e})$.
plasmafrequenz.definition: Below the plasma frequency a plasma reflects, above it it is transparent. Equality with the laser frequency defines the [[kritische-dichte|critical density]].

polarisation.kurz: Direction of oscillation of the electric field of the light wave.
polarisation.definition: Polarization can be linear, circular or elliptical. It affects absorption at oblique incidence and the orientation of [[lipss]].

preprint.kurz: Manuscript before or without peer review, e.g. on arXiv.
preprint.definition: Preprints are available early but not peer reviewed. If possible cite the peer-reviewed version.

pulsabstand.kurz: Distance between two consecutive pulses on the workpiece, $d=v/f$.
pulsabstand.definition: The pulse spacing $d=v/f$ follows from scan speed $v$ and repetition rate $f$. Compared with the spot diameter $2w_0$ it determines the pulse overlap.

pulsdauer.kurz: Temporal width of the pulse (usually full width at half maximum), symbol $\tau$.
pulsdauer.definition: The pulse duration $\tau$ is the temporal width of a pulse, usually given as the full width at half maximum (FWHM).

pulsenergie.kurz: Energy of a single laser pulse, symbol $E_\mathrm{p}$, in joules.
pulsenergie.definition: The pulse energy $E_\mathrm{p}$ is the energy of a single pulse, measured in joules (usually microjoules in UKP systems). Together with [[pulsdauer]] and [[repetitionsrate]] it fixes [[spitzenleistung]] and [[mittlere-leistung]].

pulspicker.kurz: Switch that selects individual pulses from the pulse train.
pulspicker.definition: With an acousto-optic or electro-optic modulator the repetition rate of the oscillator is lowered to the process rate, or bursts are formed.

pulszug.definition: A pulse train has the average power $E_\mathrm{p}f$ and the much higher peak power $E_\mathrm{p}/\tau$.

quarzglas.definition: Fused silica is transparent from UV to near infrared and has a very low thermal expansion. It is the standard material for volume processing with fs pulses and for [[sle]].

rauheit.kurz: Short-wavelength deviation of the surface from the ideal shape, e.g. $Ra$ or $Sa$.
rauheit.definition: Profile parameters ($R$) are in ISO 21920, areal ones ($S$) in ISO 25178. Without stating filters, roughness values are not comparable.

rayleighlaenge.kurz: Distance from the focus after which the beam cross-section doubles: $z_\mathrm{R}=\pi w_0^2/(M^2\lambda)$.
rayleighlaenge.definition: The Rayleigh length $z_\mathrm{R}$ is the distance from the beam waist at which the beam radius has grown to $\sqrt2\,w_0$ (cross-section area doubled, peak fluence halved). It determines the depth of focus: $z_\mathrm{R}=\pi w_0^2/(M^2\lambda)$.

reflexion.kurz: Return of a fraction of the light at the surface, reflectance $R$.
reflexion.definition: At normal incidence on a transparent medium of refractive index $n$ the reflectance is $R=((n-1)/(n+1))^2$. Metals reflect considerably more.

repetitionsrate.kurz: Pulses per second in hertz, symbol $f$.
repetitionsrate.definition: The repetition rate $f$ states how many pulses are emitted per second. The pulse spacing is $1/f$; the [[mittlere-leistung]] is $E_\mathrm{p}\cdot f$.

resonator.kurz: Arrangement of mirrors in which the light circulates and is amplified.
resonator.definition: The cavity fixes the allowed modes. For a linear cavity of length $L$ the mode spacing is $c/(2L)$.

rissbildung.kurz: Formation of cracks by thermal or mechanical stresses.
rissbildung.definition: In laser ablation of brittle materials cracks arise from steep temperature gradients, residual stresses or pressure waves. Countermeasures: lower fluence, less heat accumulation, adapted scan strategy.

saphir.kurz: Single-crystal aluminium oxide (Al₂O₃), hard and transparent.
saphir.definition: Sapphire is a very hard, transparent single crystal used as window and substrate material; processing it is demanding because of its hardness and brittleness.

schaerfentiefe.kurz: Axial region around the focus with almost unchanged fluence, about $2z_\mathrm{R}$.
schaerfentiefe.definition: The depth of focus of the focus is of the order of $2z_\mathrm{R}$. It shrinks with the square of the focus radius.

scheibenlaser.kurz: Solid-state laser with a thin crystal disk as the gain medium.
scheibenlaser.definition: The thin disk is cooled over its large area; this allows high average power with good beam quality.

selbstfokussierung.kurz: The Kerr effect focuses an intense beam above a critical power.
selbstfokussierung.definition: The intensity is higher in the beam centre, and so is the refractive index: the medium acts like a lens. Self-focusing can destroy amplifier media and is the basis of filamentation.

selbstphasenmodulation.kurz: An intensity-dependent refractive index broadens the spectrum of a pulse.
selbstphasenmodulation.definition: Through the Kerr effect ($n=n_0+n_2I$) an intense pulse changes its own phase. This generates new frequencies and limits the pulse energy in amplifiers.

shg.kurz: Nonlinear process that doubles the frequency and halves the wavelength.
shg.definition: In a nonlinear crystal two photons of the fundamental become one of double the energy: 1030 nm becomes 515 nm. It is also the basis of [[autokorrelation|autocorrelation]].

silizium.kurz: Elemental semiconductor with an indirect band gap, standard material of microelectronics.
silizium.definition: Silicon absorbs at photon energies above the band gap and is largely transparent below it. Wafers are thinned and structured with UKP lasers.

sle.kurz: fs modification in the volume plus wet-chemical etching.
sle.definition: In selective laser etching (SLE) the material is first modified with femtosecond pulses and then etched wet-chemically; mainly in fused silica.

slm.kurz: Liquid-crystal display that shapes the phase of the beam position-dependently.
slm.definition: With an SLM, beam profiles and multiple foci can be programmed dynamically.

spallation.kurz: Layer-by-layer flaking by tensile stress after fast energy deposition.
spallation.definition: In spallation the ultrafast energy deposition creates a pressure wave that is reflected as a tensile wave and detaches material layer by layer. It is mainly discussed near the ablation threshold.

spider.kurz: Interferometric method for measuring pulse shape and phase.
spider.definition: SPIDER reconstructs the spectral phase directly from an interferogram and is suited for very short pulses.

spitzenleistung.kurz: Maximum optical power during the pulse, approximately $E_\mathrm{p}/\tau$.
spitzenleistung.definition: The peak power $P_\mathrm{peak}$ is the power at the maximum of the pulse. Approximately $P_\mathrm{peak}\approx E_\mathrm{p}/\tau$ holds; a pulse-shape factor of order 1 is neglected.

spoedigkeit.definition: Brittle materials such as glass and ceramics fail suddenly under tensile stress through crack propagation. That limits the permissible thermal and mechanical load in laser ablation.

spotdurchmesser.kurz: Diameter of the beam in the focus, usually $2w_0$ (at $1/e^2$).
spotdurchmesser.definition: The spot size is not equal to the ablated diameter: because of the threshold the crater is smaller than $2w_0$.

strahlaufweiter.kurz: Telescope that enlarges the beam radius.
strahlaufweiter.definition: A larger beam on the lens gives a smaller focus ($w_0\propto1/w_\mathrm{in}$).

strahlprofil.kurz: Spatial distribution of the intensity across the beam.
strahlprofil.definition: The beam profile is determined with a camera or the knife-edge method. Typical profiles: Gaussian, top-hat, Bessel.

strahlradius.kurz: Radius $w_0$ at which the intensity has dropped to $1/e^2$.
strahlradius.definition: The beam radius $w_0$ (based on the $1/e^2$ criterion) is the distance from the beam axis at which the intensity has dropped to $1/e^2\approx 13.5\,\%$ of the maximum. In the focus it is the focus radius.

strahltaille.kurz: Narrowest point of the beam (focus) with radius $w_0$.
strahltaille.definition: At the beam waist the wavefront is flat and the peak fluence is maximal. From there the beam widens with the [[rayleighlaenge|Rayleigh length]] as the length scale.

strecker.kurz: Dispersive arrangement that lengthens the pulse in time.
strecker.definition: The stretcher produces positive [[gdd]] and lowers the peak power before the amplifier by the stretch factor.

tastverhaeltnis.kurz: Fraction of time in which power flows, $\tau\cdot f$.
tastverhaeltnis.definition: For UKP lasers the duty cycle is tiny (e.g. $3\cdot10^{-8}$ at 300 fs and 100 kHz). It is the ratio of average to peak power.

temperaturleitfaehigkeit.kurz: Measure of how fast temperature equalizes, $D=\lambda_\mathrm{th}/(\rho c_p)$.
temperaturleitfaehigkeit.definition: The thermal diffusivity $D$ (unit m²/s) determines the [[diffusionslaenge|diffusion length]] $L_\mathrm{th}\approx\sqrt{D\tau}$.

thermalisierung.kurz: Establishment of an equilibrium distribution of the excited electrons.
thermalisierung.definition: After excitation the electrons share their energy among themselves. Only then is an electron temperature $T_\mathrm{e}$ defined.

thermoschock.kurz: Cracking caused by rapid temperature changes.
thermoschock.definition: Rapid heating creates a temperature gradient and thus thermal stress. If it exceeds the strength, the component fractures. Thermal shock resistance depends on expansion, conduction and strength.

thg.kurz: Generation of the third harmonic: wavelength divided by three.
thg.definition: From 1030 nm one obtains about 343 nm. A shorter wavelength means a smaller focus and fewer photons needed for the band gap.

ti-saphir.kurz: Solid-state laser with a very large gain bandwidth around 800 nm.
ti-saphir.definition: Because of the large bandwidth pulses of a few femtoseconds are possible. Kerr-lens mode locking is common.

transmission.kurz: Passage of light through the material.
transmission.definition: The transmission $T$ is the fraction of light that passes through the material. Transparent dielectrics have a high transmission at photon energies below the band gap.

ttm.kurz: Model with separate temperatures for electron and lattice systems.
ttm.definition: The two-temperature model (TTM) describes the electron and lattice systems with separate temperatures that exchange energy through a coupling. It is the standard model for the interaction of ultrashort pulses with metals.

ueberlapp.kurz: Fraction of the spot diameter that consecutive pulses cover jointly.
ueberlapp.definition: The linear overlap $O=1-d/(2w_0)$ describes how far consecutive spots lie on top of each other. High overlap means many pulses per spot and thus incubation and heat accumulation.

ukp.kurz: Laser pulse in the picosecond to femtosecond range.
ukp.definition: An ultrashort pulse (UKP, USP) has a duration in the picosecond to femtosecond range. The energy enters the material faster than heat can flow away (see [[ttm]]).

valenzband.kurz: Energetically low electron band that is filled at $T=0$.
valenzband.definition: The valence band holds the electrons involved in bonding. An excitation into the [[leitungsband|conduction band]] requires at least the energy of the [[bandluecke|band gap]].

verstaerker.kurz: Stage that raises the pulse energy to micro- to millijoules.
verstaerker.definition: Types: regenerative and multipass amplifiers, fibre amplifiers, thin-disk lasers. In [[cpa]] the amplifier sees the stretched pulse.

verstaerkungsmedium.kurz: Material that amplifies light by stimulated emission.
verstaerkungsmedium.definition: Examples: ytterbium-doped crystals and fibres (around 1030 nm) and titanium–sapphire (around 800 nm). The bandwidth of the medium limits the shortest pulse duration.

versuchsplanung.kurz: Systematic planning of experiments to gain a lot of information with few runs.
versuchsplanung.definition: Typical designs: factorial ($2^k$), central composite (CCD), Box–Behnken. Replicates, randomization and centre points secure the conclusions.

volumenmodifikation.kurz: Local change of the material in the interior by focused fs pulses.
volumenmodifikation.definition: In transparent materials the focus changes density, refractive index or etchability without damaging the surface. Applications: [[sle]], [[wellenleiter|waveguides]], markings.

waermeakkumulation.kurz: Rise of the temperature from pulse to pulse at a high rate.
waermeakkumulation.definition: Heat accumulation occurs when the pulse spacing is shorter than the cooling time. It enlarges the heat-affected zone and can promote melt and cracks.

wellenlaenge.kurz: Spatial distance between two equal wave phases, $\lambda=c/\nu$.
wellenlaenge.definition: The wavelength $\lambda$ is the distance between two consecutive wave crests. It is linked to the frequency by $\lambda=c/\nu$. Typical UKP wavelengths: 1030 nm (fundamental), 515 nm (SHG), 343 nm (THG).

wellenleiter.kurz: Structure with raised refractive index that guides light.
wellenleiter.definition: With fs pulses waveguides can be written directly into glass by leaving a track of slightly raised refractive index with the focus.

zeit-bandbreite-produkt.definition: Pulse duration and spectral width are coupled through the Fourier transform: $\tau\,\Delta\nu\ge K$, where $K$ depends on the pulse shape (Gaussian: $0.441$; sech²: $0.315$). Equality holds for Fourier-limited pulses without chirp.

zerstoerschwelle.kurz: Fluence above which an optic or sample is permanently damaged.
zerstoerschwelle.definition: Test methods such as 1-on-1 and S-on-1 are given in ISO 21254. The LIDT depends on pulse duration, wavelength and pulse number.
